Here's the FigDown source for this figure. It's a straightforward `block` diagram — six components, five directed connections, no branching or state — so no other genre fits better.

```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 block
title "Certificate renewal automation"

block scheduler "Scheduler"
block renewaljob "Renewal Job"
block caclient "CA Client"
block ca "Certificate Authority"
block deployagent "Deploy Agent"
block service "Service"

scheduler -> renewaljob "trigger"
renewaljob -> caclient "obtain certificate"
caclient -> ca "request certificate"
renewaljob -> deployagent "hand off"
deployagent -> service "restart"
```

Notes on the choices made:

- **Genre**: `block` — this is a small set of labeled components with directed relationships, which is exactly what `block` is for (per the router: "architecture, dataflow, hierarchy").
- **Labels kept short**: each edge label names the action in a couple of words (`trigger`, `obtain certificate`, `request certificate`, `hand off`, `restart`), leaving the surrounding prose to carry any further detail — per the mode-3 authoring rule against overstuffed labels.
- **No classes/colour** were introduced because the description gives no categorical distinction (e.g., "critical path" vs "normal") worth asserting — adding color without stated meaning would violate the "class is how meaning survives" rule.
- **All five connections** from the description are present, one-to-one, with none invented.

Next step per the normal workflow: run `node <skill-dir>/build-svg.js X.fd` to validate and produce the `.svg`, then embed both side by side in the host document with the standard source footer:

```markdown
![Certificate renewal automation: a scheduler triggers a renewal job, which obtains a new certificate via a CA client from the certificate authority, then hands off to a deploy agent that restarts the service.](figures/cert-renewal.svg)
```
